waypoints.name: Staircase Ranger Station / North Fork Skokomish Trailhead
waypoints.note: Olympic National Park wilderness permit required, booked through Recreation.gov - there are no longer paper self-registration permits at trailheads. The park entrance fee applies to park here; no Northwest Forest Pass is needed on National Park land.
waypoints.directions: From US 101 at Hoodsport, turn west on SR 119 and drive a little more than 9 miles past Lake Cushman to the T with FR 24. Turn left; the pavement ends after 1.7 miles. Continue 3.7 miles on gravel to a junction, bear right, and drive 1.2 miles to the Staircase Ranger Station, with parking across from the campground. The park entrance fee applies; no Northwest Forest Pass is needed.

waypoints.name: Spike Camp
waypoints.note: Established backcountry camp along the North Fork Skokomish River Trail on gentle old-roadbed grade; common first-night option or rest stop before the Flapjack Lakes Trail turnoff.

waypoints.name: Madeline Creek crossing
waypoints.note: Creek with small waterfalls crossed on the Flapjack Lakes Trail; last reliable water before the final steep push to the lakes basin.

waypoints.name: Black and White Lakes Trail junction
waypoints.note: Signed fork just below Flapjack Lakes where the Black and White Lakes trail splits off; stay left/straight for Flapjack Lakes.

waypoints.name: Flapjack Lakes basin
waypoints.note: Established Olympic NP backcountry camp (permit + $8/person/night, no fires); standard overnight staging spot for the Lincoln scramble.

waypoints.name: Saddle below Lincoln's north sub-peak
waypoints.note: Off-trail climb from Flapjack Lakes gains this saddle on Sawtooth Ridge; route-finding is tricky here and GPS tracks tend to drift in the boulder/brush terrain.

waypoints.name: Chockstone gully / ridge scramble section
waypoints.note: Steep (35-40+ degree) loose scree and a chockstone-choked gully with Class 3+ exposed, no-fall moves; both sides of the ridge here are steep enough to slide.

waypoints.name: Mount Lincoln
waypoints.note: True summit of Mount Lincoln, second-highest point on Sawtooth Ridge; nearby North Peak (5,690ft) and Southwest Peak (5,486ft) are separate sub-summits.
